criterionMeaning.houseEntry: No premature giant/trapped limb or Mary Ann conflation.
criterionMeaning.grownHouse: Clearly giant and one coherent body; exact window/chimney pose is separately recorded as selectedInstant.
criterionMeaning.cellar: Selected later waiting/floor-light instant, with no open bright lantern, wall-tunnel substitution or premature thieves. Earlier source-supported preparations can fail this selected-instant criterion without being globally unfaithful to the focal passage.

limits: Unblinded inspection of all attempts, not independent blind scoring. Narrow passes do not establish overall quality, identity consistency or absence of adaptation likeness. Ordinary cellar arches are not treated as proof of a criminal wall tunnel.

items.notes: Alice is a small crouching child beside the pointing Rabbit, with the cottage behind them; no premature giant body or trapped limb. This reads as receiving the errand. The clothing, house facade and pose remain generated choices; no general identity or source-fidelity approval is implied. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice crouches in the foreground while the Rabbit points, consistent with the errand before drinking. The distant house and foreground perspective do not establish giant size. No premature growth or trapped limb. House facade and Rabbit clothing differ from the baseline. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice appears as an ordinary child crouching beside the pointing Rabbit; no premature growth or trapped limb. Oversized mushrooms and a stream are unrequested scenery. Their fantasy scale is not treated as evidence that Alice herself is giant. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice is a crouching child beside the pointing Rabbit, before drinking or growing. No giant body or trapped limb. The river, mushrooms and village houses are unrequested scenery. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice is a normal child beginning to move as the Rabbit points; the errand instant is readable and there is no premature growth. Added mushrooms, stream and village scenery remain outside the narrow criterion. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice remains a child crouching next to the pointing Rabbit. Perspective with the distant cottage does not establish giant size. Several additional small rabbits appear by the cottage, and the house/costume differ from other samples; these do not create a premature-growth failure. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Clearly giant Alice fills the room, but three arms are visible: one extends through the window, one bends above her head and one rests on the floor. The raised boot presses against the outside brickwork rather than clearly entering the chimney. This combines the competing poses and fails the coherent-body criterion. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice is clearly giant, with two readable arms and two legs in a single body. The near hand hangs in front of the window sill while the other arm bends behind her head; the raised boot meets an elevated fireplace opening. Whether the arm actually passes outside and the foot is up the chimney is spatially unclear, so this is only a giant/coherent-body pass. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice is clearly giant but has three visible hand shapes: a hanging hand by the sill, a hand under her cheek and an additional hand resting over the window-side elbow. The window-side limb arrangement is not a coherent single body. The raised foot reaches the high opening, but that does not repair the extra hand or establish the requested whole pose. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Clearly giant Alice has two readable arms and two legs. This passes only the giant/coherent-body criterion. Her window-side hand rests near the sill and the raised boot braces above the wooden door, rather than establishing an arm outside and a foot up the chimney; the other arm remains above her head. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Giant Alice fills the room with a readable two-arm/two-leg body. One hand reaches the window frame and the other rests near her shoulder. The raised boot meets the stairwell/wall; the requested arm-out-window/foot-up-chimney configuration is not shown clearly. This is a narrow size/body pass only. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Alice is clearly giant but three boots/legs are visible at the right: an upper raised boot, a middle boot against the brickwork and a lower boot on the floor. The extra limb fails the coherent-body criterion. The outstretched hand braces the interior brick beside the window rather than clearly extending outside. The existing checker reported no lettering; this is not a separate systematic likeness or identity evaluation.

Four men remain exposed among labelled crates. Holmes holds an open reddish glowing lantern; the seated older man and preparations do not establish the selected late floor-light instant. The rear arch is ordinary architecture, not proof of a criminal tunnel. No emerging thieves. The foreground revolver is oversized/distorted.

Four men and labelled crates; Holmes holds an open glass lantern whose internal light is ambiguous. The older man remains seated and no distinct floor glint/opening establishes the late instant. This can read as earlier preparations; it is not evidence of a wall tunnel or premature thieves.

Four men, labelled crates and a lower-right signature. A clearly glowing open lantern beside Watson casts light across the floor; that light is not an independent glint through the floor. The older man is seated. Rear arches alone do not establish a criminal tunnel. The selected late instant fails.

Four men, with the rear man partly concealed in shadow. Holmes raises an open glass lantern with pale internal light; the older man sits visibly beside him. No distinct floor-light opening. Ordinary arches are not scored as a tunnel. Lettering remains on crates. Earlier preparations remain a possible source instant, but not the selected late one.

A bright open floor lantern lights the central passage. At least five readable men appear, with further background shadow ambiguous; no specific figure is confidently identified as a thief. The seated older man and absent distinct floor glint fail the selected instant. Crate lettering and a lower-right signature remain. Arched passages alone do not prove a criminal tunnel.

Four men, the older man seated, Holmes holding an open glass lantern with a pale interior. There is no distinct floor-light opening; this resembles earlier preparations rather than the selected concealed wait. Crate lettering remains. The arches do not establish a criminal tunnel, and no thieves emerge.

Four men, including the seated older man, with two visibly open glowing lanterns, one beside Holmes and one at the foreground edge. No distinct floor glint. Earlier preparation cues remain instead of the late concealed wait. Crate lettering remains; ordinary arches are not treated as a criminal tunnel.

Four exposed seated/crouching men, Holmes holding a lantern with visible pale flame. A tiny distant light under the rear arches is not a readable opening/glint in the foreground floor. The selected concealed wait is not established. Crate lettering and a lower-left signature remain; arches alone are not evidence of the thieves tunnel.

Four visible men, with the older man seated and Holmes lifting an open glowing lantern. Wet floor reflections do not establish the selected floor-opening glint. Crate lettering and a lower-right signature remain. Ordinary arches alone are not treated as a tunnel.

A conspicuous rough oval opening is cut through the rear brick wall, unlike the ordinary support arches. Holmes kneels by a brightly open lantern; the older man remains seated. Tiny floor flecks do not repair the selected late-instant mismatch. Four men, no clearly emerging thieves; heavy crate lettering remains.

Four men; a circular opening through the rear wall with rubble and digging tools evokes a permanent tunnel. Holmes sits beside an open lantern with visible flame. A small bright floor patch could be a glint, but the wall opening, exposed seated figures and lantern do not meet the selected late-instant criterion. Crate text and a lower-right signature remain.

Five readable men, including a shadowed man in the rear passage. Holmes holds an open glowing lantern while the older man sits beside him; no distinct floor opening/glint establishes the late instant. No specific extra man is confidently identified as a thief. Crate lettering remains. Ordinary support arches are not scored as a wall tunnel.
